partners.mechanism_chain: AKT2 (HGNC:443) —INCREASES→ PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP448); AKT1 (HGNC:442) —INCREASES→ PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP448); PIK3CA (HGNC:9535) —INCREASES→ PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP448); PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP448) —LEADS_TO→ Hypoglycemia (HP:0002158); PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP448) —LEADS_TO→ Body hemihypertrophy (HP:0002073); PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP448) —LEADS_TO→ Breast Carcinoma (HP:0002664). Gain-of-function mutations in AKT2, AKT1, and PIK3CA lead to hyperactivation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. This hyperactivation results in increased glucose uptake and utilization, contributing to hypoglycemia (Disease A), and promotes cellular growth and proliferation, leading to body hemihypertrophy (Disease A). Concurrently, dysregulation of this pathway via the same or related genes drives uncontrolled cell proliferation and survival, a hallmark of hereditary breast carcinoma (Disease B).

partners.mechanism_chain: AKT2 (HGNC:401) —DISRUPTS→ PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP449); PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP449) —DECREASES→ Insulin secretion; Insulin secretion —LEADS_TO→ Hypoglycemia (HP:0002070); AKT2 (HGNC:401) —LEADS_TO→ Hemihypertrophy (HP:0002153); AKT1 (HGNC:397) —DISRUPTS→ PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP449); PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP449) —INCREASES→ Cell growth and proliferation; Cell growth and proliferation —LEADS_TO→ Somatic overgrowth; Somatic overgrowth —LEADS_TO→ Hemihypertrophy (HP:0002153).
